subject: Multistate model with two unobserved states (one partially observed)

messages.author: 0b13e958dd74a539
messages.subject: Multistate model with two unobserved states (one partially observed)
parts:
I'd appreciate any help with the following problem. I'm testing a multistate model in which fish can disappear either because of natural mortality or undetected emigration from the study area. I have a second likelihood component for estimating the probability of undetected emigration. Despite that added information, all fish that disappear end up being classified as natural deaths.  Full R/JAGS code is attached as a text file, but the key aspects are as follows:

Fish in this model have four true and four observed states:

 True states
 1. Alive
 2. Harvest
 3. Natural death
 4. Emigrant

 Observed states
 1. Detection of live fish (time-dependent probability p_t)
 2. Detection of harvest (probability 1)
 3. Detected emigration (probability p_emig)
 4. Not detected

The transition probabilities for true states allow live fish to transition into either of the remaining three true states (which are terminal).

With this design, fish can disappear in one of two ways: natural death and undetected emigration.  I thought the second likelihood component for the probability of detecting emigration (a binomial experiment) would allow fish that disappear to be allocated between natural death and undetected emigration. But all fish that disappear are classified as natural deaths.

The specific example I am testing is for 30 fish, with true fates as follows:

Alive to end of study     5
Harvest 5
Natural death 10
Detected emigration 5
Undetected emigration 5

My thinking was that the probability of detecting emigration (0.5) was reliably estimated by the second likelihood component, so the model would infer that there were about 5 undetected emigrants to match the 5 detected emigrants. Thus in theory, the number of natural deaths would be approximately correct because all the other categories were reliably estimated or known.

One last note: the model is struggling to achieve convergence on the true (latent) state of fish that disappear.

Is there a different way to structure the model that would improve its performance? Thanks for any insights.

Joe Hightower

messages.author: 536408d0b025f968
messages.subject: Re: Multistate model with two unobserved states (one partially observed)
parts:
Dear Joe,

I have several questions about the design of your model and some suggestions.
i think the problem is in the state matrix. Maybe you should try to rewrite your model.
Usually, when dealing with individuals alive and dead, you need to have incremental dead states: Alive, newly/just dead and Dead to distinguish when you die and once you're dead. You can find some examples of studies with several causes of death (Schaub & Pradel 2004 Ecology, Souchay & Schaub 2016 PLoS ONE).
So, in your case, you should have the following state :
Alive (A)
Permanent emigration (PE)
Newly dead - Harvest  (NdH)
newly dead - Natural    (NdN)
Dead (D)

thus, you should have the following matrice for state transition
            A         PE      NdH       NdN     D
A       F*S      (1-F)    F*mH   F* mN     0 
PE       0           1          0              0       0
NdH     0           0         0              0       1
NdN     0           0         0              0       1
D          0           0         0              0       1
with F = the probability to stay in the studied area (look at standard CMR book to get more information about Fidelity to study area, see section 9.5.1 of Kery & Schaub book), S = the survival prob being 1 - mH - mN (so 1- all mortality rate), mH = mortality rate due to Harvest, mN = mortality rate due to Natural cause of death.
I think your model will be clearer and easier to understand. With this description, you can have a parameter for individuals staying inside the studied area and those emigrating, so now you should be able to get individual emigrating and those dying from natural causes.
See section 9.6 for the use of the multinomial link function or the dirichlet priors

And the associated matrice for detection should be
          1       2          3         4   
A        p       0         0          1-p
PE     0   p_emig    0    1-p_emig
NdH   0      0          1           0
NdN   0      0          0          1
D        0      0          0          1
with 1 = detected alive; 2 = detected emigrated; 3 = recovered harvest; 4 = not detected
are you sure that you can detect all dead individuals with your sampling design?
 
Cheers,

Guillaume

messages.author: 0b13e958dd74a539
messages.subject: Re: Multistate model with two unobserved states (one partially observed)
parts:
Hi Guillaume (and list),

Thank you for responding and providing some good suggested changes. Unfortunately the issue still persists even with those changes (discrete rather than instantaneous rates, modeling fidelity separately, using incremental dead states). The model was still unable to sort out natural mortality (never detected) from emigration (detected with well-estimated or even fixed probability p_emig).  I find that surprising, especially with fixed p_emig, but this is obviously a data-limited situation. Thanks again for taking time to provide feedback.

Joe
